signals.evidence: Grade 12 students preparing for summer matriculation exams after ceasefire declaration, attempting to close gaps and succeed in exams following years of crises (Corona, Gaza operations, teacher strikes, October 7 war)

Dr. Dana Livneh, urologist at Meir Medical Center: approximately 10 adolescents aged 12-18 diagnosed with testicular torsion in recent month; three lost testicles; rate of 30%+ testicular loss vs. professional literature rate of 7-10%, attributed to late arrival at emergency room due to war effects
Dozens of extreme Haredi protesters demonstrating outside IDF recruitment offices in Tel HaShomer and Jerusalem against conscription of young Haredim; protesters attempting to block recruits' paths

Kiryat Shmona Mayor Avihai Stern: 'They determine our future in Washington instead of Jerusalem... our fate was placed in the hands of the Israeli government, called it "right on full." I haven't spoken with the Defense Minister or Prime Minister since the war began. After more than 40 days in shelters, at least there should be a clear result - dismantling Hezbollah and quiet for generations.' Matzuba Council Head: 'We are in terrible tension. They don't listen to the IDF - there are no cannons.'

Business owners have not received a single shekel in compensation for revenue decline of at least 25% during war; Treasury framework passed only first reading in Knesset, not yet final approval; many businesses facing severe liquidity difficulties and risk of closure and bankruptcy

Attorney Ayelet HaShachar Saidoff, 'Mothers at the Front' organization: 'We, mothers of fighters and soldiers, are fed up. Our sons are wounded, they have no right to normal lives. Where is it heard that one mother is condemned to a life of anxiety and another to a good life? Those who violate the rights of soldiers are also you [judges].'

Ayelet HaShachar Saidoff, founder of 'Mothers at the Front,' representing approximately 100,000 mothers of soldiers: 'The court is dragging its feet. We, mothers of fighters and soldiers, are fed up! 914 days of fighting, fed up with dragging feet, fed up with answers of reserve duty support, fed up.'

18-year-old Abraham Yeshayahu Spiegel missing since entering water at Tzanz Beach in Netanya; his brother Yissachar Dov (21) in serious condition hospitalized at Laniado Hospital; family waiting and hoping for good news after three days of search
17-year-old yeshiva student from Bnei Brak found dead in Ein Akev spring in Negev after drowning; located after hours of search by Lahav unit divers of Fire and Rescue Authority

Ashkelon Mayor Tomer Glam: 'This year, in light of the fragile ceasefire and security instability, we are required to make difficult decisions. We decided painfully to postpone Independence Day celebrations and not hold the central Memorial Day ceremony... while our fighters stand at the front in different enemy zones and our brothers and sisters in the north are still under fire, we feel it is not right to celebrate and put tens of thousands of people at risk.'

Resident: 'I received 500 shekels per person from the municipality - is that enough to buy a child who lost everything clothes? A computer? It's illogical. The municipality is trying to help, but I feel it is limited compared to the state, which doesn't really care about us.'

Displaced resident: 'We are experiencing the shit of life, and it's absurd that those supporting us are citizens, each one of them an angel extending a hand, but the state doesn't really treat us. The municipality is trying to help, but I feel it is limited compared to the state.'

Cycling trail 'Bor Bari' in Gaza envelope reopened to public after being closed military zone since October 7; 11 cyclists killed on October 7 on this trail; reopening represents resumption of normal recreational activity

Arez Manor, cycling center manager at Kibbutz Bari: 'It's moving... Like they say 'the wheat is growing again,' here too, it's a victory of spirit over everything.' Simon King, Bari resident since 1984: 'This trail is in my eyes one of the most beautiful in the world... It's very moving to see families coming to the trail I built with my friends and enjoying it. It gives me a lot of satisfaction and symbolizes resilience.'

Education system returning to near-full routine; in northern front line areas and Haifa Bay, gradual opening beginning Sunday under Home Front Command restrictions requiring studies only in protected spaces; approximately 80% of students returned, while 20% struggling to adjust to return to study routine

Children returning to schools but showing signs of anxiety: regression in behavior, separation difficulties, new fears, sleep disorders; particularly difficult for children with special needs; one month and a half of running to shelters, lack of sleep, and clinging to parents does not disappear in one day
15 Haredim arrested during illegal protest near IDF recruitment office in Kiryat Ono; protesters attempted to block vehicles by lying on road; protesters called police 'Nazis'

Judge Chachlai sentenced two kindergarten teachers to jail and fines for abuse of toddlers; investigation revealed hundreds of cases of severe abuse documented in security camera footage over two months; children exposed to physical and psychological violence including hitting, pulling hair, throwing in air, slamming into chairs and mattresses

Grade 12 students in northern front line areas demanding improved relief framework for matriculation exams from Education Ministry; school principals demanding focused response for classes where teachers are on extended reserve duty; Education Ministry published partial material focusing and limited relief, declining broader framework due to concerns about exam quality

Hospitals Rambam, Bnei Zion, and Carmel in northern Israel conducting gradual transition from underground to above-ground operations; Pediatrics, Obstetrics, and Neonatology departments returned to regular facilities; full readiness maintained to return to underground operations within hours if needed; Rambam treated over 8,000 patients in underground facility during fighting

IDF admits shortage of 9,000 fighters in field; warns shortage will jump to 17,000 by end of year without urgent legislation; enforcement against draft evaders nearly halted due to diversion of military police to combat missions in 'Roaring Lion' operation

IDF reduced enforcement against draft evaders significantly in recent 1.5 months due to diversion of military police to combat-related missions; military police reassigned to Home Front Command reinforcement at impact zones and manning checkpoints on northern border

Magen David Adom staff and volunteers meeting with 90-year-old Holocaust survivor Rachel Golani as part of 'Memory at the Station' project; survivor sharing story of five years in Siberian labor camp from age 3 and post-Holocaust rehabilitation

598 million shekels paid today to approximately 100,000 unemployed; approximately 70,000 continuing cases and 30,000 new claims from war; National Insurance reporting high volume of additional pending requests with approximately 96,000 new claims filed in recent days, mostly after Passover holiday

Golan Regional Council announced that school day opened as planned Sunday across entire council including northern Golan Heights; council clarified that explosions heard in area stem from fighting in Upper Galilee, not Golan sector; Operations Center monitoring school day with ongoing situation assessments

Tel Hai University in Kiryat Shmona reopened academic studies Sunday after more than one month delay, similar to most higher education institutions in Israel; studies conducted remotely due to security situation on northern border; over 4,700 students enrolled; approximately 15% of students currently on active reserve duty; approximately 40% of registered students chose to remain and reside in Upper Galilee and Golan communities despite operation against Iran and Hezbollah

Asher Gat, father of murdered hostage Carmel Gat: 'Today I witnessed the demolition of my home, evacuation of entire lives that were violently cut short. The memories remain in my soul, I hold onto them every day, but the house is not a symbol or memorial site. We will continue the path that was cut off for them through a social-experiential initiative commemorating the lives of Carmel and Kinneret, who were women of action, doing, and love of the land. I hope as many people as possible will come to run and walk in their paths.'

Reservists Party launched first physical headquarters in Kiryat Shmona amid ongoing fighting and tension with Lebanon; headquarters serves as center for civilian and political activity including operating support command center for northern residents, holding meetings and briefings, and maintaining ongoing presence; party representatives met with northern municipal leaders

Children returned to frameworks after 1.5 months of alerts, fragmented sleep, and lack of routine; body and mind still tense; one month and a half of running to shelters and lack of sleep do not disappear in one day; many children showing regression in behavior, separation difficulties, new fears, sleep disorders; particularly difficult for children with special needs; regression not trivial and will not disappear within week of returning to kindergarten, possibly not within months

Blue Bird Airways scheduled to depart Ben Gurion for Athens at 10:30, becoming first foreign airline to depart after ceasefire; El Al began operating flights to approximately 30 destinations today including Rome, Warsaw, Munich, Amsterdam, Paris, London

Children of northern front line have not returned to routine despite ceasefire; harsh reality of alerts, explosions, and zero warning time continues; children very young but also very mature for their age, describing how they see reality of war against Hezbollah

El Al expanding operations to approximately 40 destinations starting April 19 from current 30; weekly flight volume expected to reach approximately 660 flights; new destinations include Boston, Krakow, London (Luton), Marseille, Paphos, Rhodes, Thessaloniki, Tivat Montenegro, and Sofia; company setting price caps for all destinations through end of August

Health Ministry issuing guidelines today to all hospitals nationwide for gradual expansion of operations; guidelines designed to enable continuity of care while maintaining strict safety for patients and medical teams; approximately 7,000 wounded treated in hospitals since Operation 'Roaring Lion' began; significant portion of wounded injured during descent to protected spaces rather than from direct missile strikes

Kadumim local council preparing for day after ceasefire and continuing strengthening of protected spaces in community; total of nine shelters to be deployed at central points in settlement as part of efforts to improve resident preparedness for emergency events; council head Uzal Vatik: 'After extensive work with Defense Ministry and Home Front Command, we succeeded in bringing additional shelters to Kadumim. Resident security always stands at top of our priorities.'

Health Ministry updated that gradual return of Haifa hospitals from underground to above-ground operations underway; Rambam, Bnei Zion, and Carmel conducting gradual and controlled transition while maintaining full readiness to return to underground operations within hours if needed

Employment Service reports: number of active job seekers in Israel increased this week by approximately 18% (addition of 54,898 citizens) and stands at 359,533 compared to 304,635 active job seekers reported previous week; total workers placed on unpaid leave since operation began stands at 164,210 citizens - increase of approximately 41.3% (addition of 47,993 placed on unpaid leave) compared to previous week (116,217)
יהושע שרמן (אביו של דניאל): 'יש עוד תהליך ארוך של שיקום, דרך ארוכה לפניו, אבל שמחים על מה שיש... בתוך כל האסון הגדול הזה יש ניסים גדולים'
בית החולים נאלצו הרופאים לקבוע את מותו של יהודה שמואל
משרד הבריאות מודיע כי מתבצעת חזרה הדרגתית של בתי החולים בחיפה מפעילות בתת-קרקע לפעילות מעל הקרקע
באזור המפרץ, עבר ממדרג של פעילות מצומצמת למדרג פעילות חלקית, המאפשר חזרה מסוימת למסלול לצד הדריכות הביטחונית
רשת 'פרח ישראל' שבו לפעילות שגרה מלאה כל מוסדות הרשת עם הכרזת הפסקת האש
רשות שדות התעופה הודיעה על חידוש הדרגתי של שירות 'פטור ושמור' בנמל התעופה בן גוריון
חברות תעופה זרות חוזרות לפעילות בנמל התעופה בן גוריון: VBB, Tus Airways, Etihad Airways, Ethiopian Airlines, Hainan Airlines, Red Wings Georgian Airways, FlyOne
אמילי עמרוסי: 'אני בקבוצה הקטנה של כמה רבבות בודדות של ישראלים שנפלה בחלקם הזכות להיות הורים של בוני המקדש... מה היא אומרת לו ב-60 שניות לפני שלוקחים לו את הטלפון ולה את החמצן ל-30 עד 60 יום'
שופטת יעל וילנר: 'יש פערים אדירים באכיפה בין הציבור הלא חרדי לחרדי. זה לא להאמין הפערים. איפה השוויון'
דائرة التشغيل בישראל: ארתפاع בנسבה של 18% בעדד הבוחשים על עבודה, ל-359,533 אנשים, עם 55 אלף שהצטרפו בשבוע אחד בלבד
אלפים הפגינו נגד הממשלה ונגד מלחמת איראן בתל אביב, חרגו מגבולות שנקבעו בפסק דין
26 high-tech companies and venture capital funds stepped in to help enable participation by Holocaust survivors aged 90-100 in the March of the Living
Nine foreign carriers expected to gradually resume flight services to and from Tel Aviv's Ben Gurion Airport this week

Transportation Minister Miri Regev: 'We are making efforts to expand air activity and return the aviation industry to full operations. The return of foreign airlines will allow the Israeli public to once again fly to a wider variety of destinations and increase the supply of flights.'
Kibbutz members voted to demolish all but one destroyed home, deciding that rebuilding rather than living in a perpetual monument to the attack was crucial in allowing them to move on
Adults and children from local Arab community attended Orthodox Easter service at the Holy Sepulchre, wearing best outfits, taking family pictures, and exchanging Easter greetings
Phethen from Jerusalem: 'We wait for this moment the whole year. It's happy to be here, but the situation still feels hard. It's not like every other year.'
Xenia, 35, from Russia: 'I had never come here for Easter, but after everything that has happened, I want to take advantage of every opportunity for normal life that I have'
Ex-hostage Braslavski noticed elderly Arab construction workers working long hours outside his building and decided to buy them soda and cigarettes, speaking to them in Arabic
Ex-hostage Braslavski received countless angry messages from fellow Israelis after posting about treating Arabs with respect
Residents in shelters formed new friendships, shared stories on social media, organized a matza bake, and opened a grocery store in one shelter
Residents in shelters get rare quality time with neighbors, balancing work and family life while sheltering together

AI-psychological first aid (AI-PFA) app developed at Ben-Gurion University provides immediate, science-backed intervention for shock and anxiety victims in the field, available in English, Hebrew, and Arabic
Ben-Gurion University study: 40% of teachers reported levels of anxiety and depression that crossed clinical thresholds; 12% suffered from severe depression and 5% from severe anxiety

Magen 48 trains civilian first responder teams in Be'eri to prepare local responders for future attacks, founded by counterterrorism trainer Dribben after concluding trained civilian teams made the difference between communities that held out and those overrun

Residents experiencing accumulated stress from intense moments of running to shelters day and night, sounds of interceptions and impacts, exposure to tragedies and stressful news, lack of routine, with very high levels of adrenaline, cortisol, and other stress hormones
Islands of returning to routine are emerging across different regions of the country, with partial return of educational frameworks signaling some stability

Daniel Sherman, severely injured in ramming attack that killed his brother: 'He is walking on two feet, which wasn't certain at all. With this great tragedy, there are also great miracles. There is great joy and thanks to G-d'
